chunks: Do not revile those who invoke others apart from God, lest they begin to revile God out of malice and ignorance. We have made attractive their deeds to every people. They have to go back to their Lord, when He will tell them what they used to do.
ai.seo_question: Why should Muslims avoid insulting the idols of polytheists?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (Ayat al-Dhikr) is often cited to justify respectful dialogue with other faiths, emphasizing that provoking anger leads to irrational blasphemy born of ignorance rather than theological conviction. It highlights the divine wisdom in making each community's deeds appealing to them, serving as a test before their ultimate return to Allah for accountability.
